title: Rate limiting for the Orders API, line by line
subtitle: feature/rate-limit → main · simple style

scenes.narration: This change does three things. It limits how many orders one address can send per minute. It prices each item from the pricing service. And it sends an event for every new order. There are no tests.
scenes.summary: Limit POST /orders to 20 per minute per IP, price items from the pricing service, and publish order.created.
bullets: If Redis is down, every order request fails
The event is sent after the save, so a queue error fails a saved order
No tests cover the limiter, the prices, or the event

scenes.narration: Here is the system. A client calls the orders API. The API asks Redis, a fast shared store, to count the request. The orders service saves the order. Then the API tells the queue.

steps.say: First the API counts the request in Redis.
Then the create order function prices the items and saves the order.
Last, the API sends the new order event and does not wait for a reader. Then the API answers the client.

scenes.title: POST /orders
scenes.narration: Here is the data at each step.

steps.say: The limiter counts the request.
The service prices every item.
Then the service saves the order.
The API sends a small event about the order.
Then the API answers the client.

scenes.narration: Before the change, look at the database client. The orders service uses the database client to save orders. This file does not change.

steps.say: Line one defines the database client.
The insert function takes a table name and a row. Insert gives back the row with a new id.

scenes.narration: This is the new rate limit file. The file has one function. Let us read it from the top.

steps.say: Line one imports the request types from Express. Line two imports the Redis client. Redis is a fast store for small values.
Lines four and five start the options. The window is the length of one time window, in milliseconds.
Line six is the maximum. The maximum is the number of requests allowed in one window. Line seven closes the options.
Line nine defines the rate limit function. The function takes the options. Line ten returns a middleware. A middleware is a function that runs before the route.

scenes.narration: Now the body of the middleware. The middleware runs once for every request to the orders route. First it counts the request.
scenes.calloutText: The key expires with the window, so Redis cleans it up.

steps.say: Line eleven builds a key. The key has the IP address and the current minute. So each address gets a new key every minute.
steps.label: Build a key for this address and minute

steps.say: Line twelve adds one to the count for that key in Redis. Redis returns the new count.
steps.label: Count the request in Redis

steps.say: Line thirteen runs only on the first request in a window. Line thirteen tells Redis to delete the key after one minute.
steps.label: On the first hit, expire the key after a minute

scenes.narration: The count decides what happens next.
scenes.calloutText: Retry-After tells the client how many seconds to wait.

steps.say: Line fourteen checks the count. The maximum is twenty. So the check is true from request number twenty-one on.
steps.label: Is the count over the limit?

steps.say: Line fifteen adds a header that tells the client to wait sixty seconds. Line sixteen answers with status four twenty-nine. That status means too many requests.
steps.label: Refuse with Retry-After and 429

steps.say: Line seventeen closes the check. Line eighteen passes the request on to the route.
steps.label: Under the limit, pass the request on

steps.say: Lines nineteen and twenty close the middleware and the function.
steps.label: End of the function

scenes.narration: This is the server file. Four lines are new.
scenes.calloutText: publish runs after the insert, so a queue error fails a saved order.

steps.say: Line three imports the rate limit function.
Line four imports the publish function from the queue module.
Line eight puts the limiter on the orders path. The window is sixty thousand milliseconds, which is one minute. The maximum is twenty.
Line twelve runs after the order is saved. Line twelve sends an order created event with the order id and the total.

scenes.narration: This is the orders service. The service used a fixed price of ten. Now the service asks the pricing service.
scenes.calloutText: Pricing lookups run in parallel with Promise.all.

steps.say: Line two imports the function that looks up a price.
The old lines nine and ten are removed. The old lines priced every item at ten and saved the order.
The new line ten refuses an empty order. Line ten throws an error.
Line eleven asks the price of each item. All the price lookups run at the same time.
Line twelve adds up quantity times price for each item. The sum is the total.
Line thirteen saves the order with the total and a status of pending.

scenes.narration: This is the new queue module.

steps.say: The publish function takes a topic and the data to send. Today the function only logs them. A real queue would come later.

scenes.narration: This old file is deleted. Nothing imported it any more.

steps.say: The old throttle kept a count for each key in memory.
The old throttle allowed up to one hundred hits per key. Memory is lost on restart, so Redis replaces the throttle.

scenes.narration: This change adds no tests. Nothing checks the limit, the prices, or the event. The screen lists what is missing.
gaps: The twenty first request in a minute from one IP gets 429 with a Retry-After header
When Redis is down the limiter throws, so every order request fails
When the queue is down after the insert, the client gets an error for a saved order
Empty orders are rejected and totals use prices from the pricing service
